stories.headline: Cyclone Akvan impact: 20 flights cancelled at Ranchi airport due to bad weather
stories.title: Cyclone Akvan impact: 20 flights cancelled at Ranchi airport due to bad weather
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Ranchi: As many as 20 flights were cancelled at the Birsa Munda Airport here on Saturday due to inclement weather triggered by cyclone 'Akvan', an official said.
Jharkhand has been experiencing cloudy weather coupled with light rain since Friday under the influence of the cyclone.
For safe landing or take-off, a visibility between 1,200 and 1,500 metres is required.
"The visibility at Ranchi airport was around 1,000 metres until 1pm," Airport Director Vinod Kumar told PTI.
In all, 20 scheduled flights were cancelled due to bad weather, including six Air India Express flights, an airport official said.
In addition, four flights were diverted due to inclement weather.
The state's weather is likely to improve from Sunday with clearing of clouds, an IMD official said.
"We are expecting the weather to improve from Sunday with dense fog in the morning hours.
A clear sunshine is likely from November 23," Baburaj PP, director at Ranchi Meteorological Centre, told PTI.
Chaibasa Sadar in West Singbhum district recorded highest rainfall at 34.4 mm during the past 24 hours till 8.30am on Saturday.
Ghatsila in East Singhbhum district registered 32.6 mm rainfall, Simega 28.2mm, Jamshedpur 22.2 mm and Ranchi recorded 12.4 mm rainfall.

The maximum temperature is likely to remain unchanged for the next 24 hours in the state and thereafter it will start rising by 6 degree Celsius during the next three days, according to the weather bulletin.

stories.headline: Skill development linked to national security, defence production: Rajnath Singh
stories.title: Skill development linked to national security, defence production: Rajnath Singh
stories.summary: Lucknow, Nov 21: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Saturday said skill development is no longer limited to generating employment and is crucial for nation-building and national security, citing the example of India's growing defence production sector. Addressing the fifth National Skill Convocation here, Singh said the country's industries are expanding, and the nature of employment is undergoing transformation, making it essential for young people to continuously upgrade their skills. "Today, the importance of skill development is not limited to securing employment. It is connected with nation-building and national security. An important example of this is our defence production," he said. Singh said under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, industries are growing, and the methods of working are changing rapidly. "In such a situation, merely acquiring skills is not enough. It is also extremely important to keep up with the times. Therefore, our government is making efforts to ensure that skills of young people develop continuously through skilling, reskilling and upskilling initiatives," he said. The defence minister said the economic strength of a country is determined not merely by its natural resources, capital or technological advancement but also by the capabilities and skills of its citizens. "In our tradition, we have learnt that knowledge gives a person understanding, skills give them capability, and a combination of both makes them self-reliant," he said. Singh said the National Skill Convocation has helped change the perception that convocation ceremonies are associated primarily with universities and higher academic degrees. "Skill development is in no way inferior to formal education. Rather, it supplements and complements it," he asserted. Highlighting the expansion of the country's skill development ecosystem over the past 12 years, Singh said more than 1.64 crore young people have received training under the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) till June 2026. He said the number of Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) in the country has increased from approximately 9,800 in 2014 to more than 14,000 at present. However, he said, the significance of these figures lay in the transformation that skill development had brought to the lives of young people. "When a young person from a small town or village receives training from an ITI and starts working in an industry, they do not merely earn a livelihood but also transform the economic condition of their family," he said. Similarly, a young person who establishes an enterprise using technical skills not only creates employment for themselves, but also generates opportunities for others, contributing to the goal of self-reliance, he added. Singh said a strong skill ecosystem has been made possible through the vision of Prime Minister Modi, who recognised that skills need to be developed in mission mode to realise the goal of a developed India. He said skill development has progressed at an unprecedented pace over the past 12 years. Singh also congratulated the 52 national-level toppers from Industrial Training Institutes, National Skill Training Institutes and Institutes of Training of Trainers who were felicitated by Prime Minister Modi at the ceremony. He said the fifth National Skill Convocation is a special occasion as it is being held outside Delhi for the first time. Congratulating Union Minister of State for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship Jayant Chaudhary for organising the national-level programme in Lucknow, Singh also described it as a matter of pride for Uttar Pradesh and congratulated Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. The event was attended by Narendra Modi, Yogi Adityanath, Jayant Chaudhary and other senior dignitaries and officials. Singh, who represents Lucknow in the Lok Sabha, earlier welcomed the prime minister to the Uttar Pradesh capital and extended his greetings to young achievers who had arrived from different parts of the country.

stories.headline: China yet to share info on camera recovered from Pahalgam massacre terrorists: NIA
stories.title: China yet to share info on camera recovered from Pahalgam massacre terrorists: NIA
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 21: China has not yet responded to India's request regarding a US-manufactured GoPro camera recovered from the terrorists behind last year's Pahalgam massacre, NIA DG Rakesh Aggarwal said on Friday, asserting that investigators have gathered "some forensic evidence" in the case. "We have not received any reply so far… But we have some forensic evidence," Aggarwal told reporters here when asked if the agency had received any communication from Chinese authorities regarding the device. During the investigation into the Pahalgam terror attack, investigators had aggressively made attempts to trace a global supply chain to determine how the camera supplied to China ended up in the hands of the Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) terror outfit, senior officials said. The high-tech camera, recovered from the terrorists who were neutralised in an encounter in the Dachigam forests in July last year following the attack, has opened a critical new line of inquiry into the external logistics network supporting terror outfits in Jammu and Kashmir. Terror groups in the Union territory have increasingly been using body-worn and tactical cameras to record their ambushes for propaganda and psychological warfare. Investigators believe that unearthing this specific supply chain could expose critical vulnerabilities or complicity in the underground networks that funnel funds, hardware and tactical gear across borders to anti-India outfits. In a bid to uncover the device's origin, the National Investigation Agency (NIA) officially reached out to the US manufacturer GoPro Inc to ascertain where the camera had been sold and the company replied that the specific device was originally shipped to an authorised commercial distributor in China, according to the officials. Officials familiar with the developments said the probe has now shifted focus toward tracking how the camera moved from the Chinese distributor to LeT handlers, with investigators examining the strong possibility that the devices were procured by the Pakistan Army and subsequently supplied to terror groups. Because India does not have a Mutual Legal Assistance Treaty (MLAT) with China, requests for information in such cases are pursued through diplomatic channels. As many as 26 people, mainly tourists, were gunned down by terrorists in the Baisaran meadows of Pahalgam on April 22, 2025. The massacre prompted New Delhi to launch 'Operation Sindoor', targeting terror infrastructure in Pakistan-controlled territories, including the main camps of the banned LeT and Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM). The three terrorists involved in the Pahalgam attack were later killed in an encounter with Army special forces in the Dachigam forests on the outskirts of Srinagar. At least two AK-47 rifles recovered from the Baisaran attack site, as well as one from the Dachigam encounter site, also had their origin in China, officials noted. According to preliminary investigations, the three terrorists escaped from the Baisaran meadows through the Pahalgam jungles and likely fled in a vehicle, capitalising on a nearly 40-minute window before security forces could fully grasp the magnitude of the attack. While a vehicle bearing a Shopian registration number was spotted on a road leading out of Pahalgam, investigators lost its trail as several CCTV cameras along the route were malfunctioning. The NIA has filed a chargesheet against the LeT outfit and six individuals, including the three killed terrorists, identified as Faisal Jatt alias Suleman, Habeeb Tahir alias Chottu, and Hamza Afghani, and self-styled LeT "commander" Sajid Jatt alias Sajid Jutt. Investigators are still ascertaining whether additional operatives were involved in the conspiracy. Two local residents, Bashir Ahmad Jothatd and Parvaiz Ahmad, were also named in the chargesheet for providing food and shelter to the terrorists for five hours a day prior to the attack.

stories.headline: J'khand CM Soren writes to CJI seeking urgent appointment of HC chief justice successor
stories.title: J'khand CM Soren writes to CJI seeking urgent appointment of HC chief justice successor
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'chief justice' in title weight 42
article_sentences: Surya Kant and the Supreme Court Collegium, urging them to expedite the appointment of a successor to Jharkhand High Court Chief Justice M S Sonak, who is due to retire on November 27.

In his letter to the CJI and Collegium members, Soren warned that the absence of a permanent successor could lead to another interim arrangement, affecting administrative continuity and institutional planning in the high court, as cited by PTI.

“Without the Collegium's immediate action, the High Court of Jharkhand faces the prospect of yet another interim Acting Chief Justice arrangement… I hope it (the Collegium) will not disagree with me that the office of the Chief Justice is central to the administrative and judicial functioning of a high court,” he wrote.

Soren also stressed the need for stable judicial leadership to maintain public confidence in the justice delivery system, saying frequent leadership transitions could disrupt the functioning of the institution.
